exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study included 486 postpartum women (243 vaginal and 243 cesarean deliveries) recruited from a maternity ward.
finding: Women who gave birth by cesarean section generally reported higher satisfaction scores but also showed a higher tendency to avoid pregnancy, while birth memory and recall characteristics were more pronounced in women who gave birth vaginally.
mod_finding: Women delivering by cesarean section reported higher childbirth satisfaction and a greater tendency to avoid pregnancy compared to those with vaginal births, who instead exhibited more pronounced birth memory and recall.
